function: MIMO channel estimation from few pilots (pilot density below 1): a learned diffusion score prior with variational inference recovers the channel matrix (p. 1, p. 3).
system: Point-to-point MIMO, ULA 128x32 and UPA 256x64 antennas, no RIS, 40 GHz carrier, 3GPP CDL channels (p. 8, Table I; p. 10-11).
method: U-Net score network, unsupervised denoising score matching; variance-exploding diffusion prior used in variational inference with Dirac posterior, no retraining per pilot or SNR (p. 6-7).
data_channel: Channels generated with MATLAB 5G Toolbox CDL-A/B/C/D (3GPP TR 38.901); 10000 training and 100 test channels per CDL profile (p. 8).
test_conditions: Trained per CDL profile or on a mixed set; tested on the same and on other profiles (CDL-C model on CDL-A/B/D), SNR -10 to 30 dB (p. 9).
baselines: ML, EM-GM-AMP (compressive sensing), LDAMP (deep unfolding), Langevin posterior sampling with score model, Wasserstein GAN, approximate MMSE upper bound (p. 9).
metrics: NMSE in dB versus SNR, pilot density and antenna size; 3x inference speed-up over Langevin; FLOPs, latency, memory, model size (p. 8, p. 12-13).
complexity: Table II, Nr=16, Nt=64: 307.4 GFLOPs, 232 ms, 3.4e6 parameters, 6.5 MB; Langevin 986.5 GFLOPs, 720 ms; LDAMP 6.3 GFLOPs (p. 13).
openness: none (the only link is the public MATLAB code of the EM-GM-AMP baseline, p. 13).
q1_support: p. 8: "all channel realizations for training and testing are generated using the clustered delay line (CDL) family of channel models in the 5G Toolbox in MATLAB following the 3GPP specifications TR 38.901"
q2_support: p. 9: "using the diffusion model trained on CDL-C to estimate CDL-A channels show poor performance" (a CDL-C model is also tested on CDL-B and CDL-D, and a mixed-trained model on each profile).
q3_support: p. 9: "Maximum Likelihood (ML) [3]" (non-learned) and "LDAMP [21]: LDAMP is a powerful deep unfoldingbased method" (earlier learned estimator); the Langevin score-based [34] and W-GAN [23] estimators are also compared in NMSE (Fig. 2).
q4_support: p. 13: "inference floating-point operations (FLOPs), latency, memory footprints, and model size" (Table II lists 307.4G FLOPs, 232 ms and 3.4 x 10^6 parameters for the proposed method).
q5_support: p. 8: "all channel realizations for training and testing are generated using the clustered delay line (CDL) family of channel models in the 5G Toolbox in MATLAB"; no code or data link of its own, the only URL is a baseline (p. 13: "relies on the publicly available MATLAB code").
notes: Included, area 2. CDL via the MATLAB 5G Toolbox following TR 38.901 is read as a standard channel (q1). The antenna-size sweep trains a separate model per size (p. 12), so q2 rests on the cross-profile tests of p. 9 and Fig. 2. The approximate MMSE bound is computed with the proposed method itself, so it is not counted as a baseline. Tables I and II were read from the page images (p. 8, p. 13).
